title: How to Calculate Your Real Estate Salary: Hourly to Annual for a 38-Hour Week
description: Convert your hourly rate to an annual real estate salary using a 38-hour week, 52-week year. Includes tax, super, and fortnightly pay estimates.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, your annual real estate salary is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 then by 52, before tax and super.

faqs.q: Does the real estate salary industry average include casual loading?
faqs.a: No. The rental, hiring and real estate industry average of $1979.6 per week (from the ABS, May 2026) is for full-time adult ordinary time earnings. It does not include casual loading. If you are a casual employee, your hourly rate should already include the 25% casual loading, and the average would be higher. Use our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) guide to check your rate.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on a real estate salary?
faqs.a: Super is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026). For example, if your annual real estate salary is $80,000, your employer adds $9,600 in super, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This is not deducted from your pay. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more.

faqs.q: What tax will I pay on my real estate salary?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, resident tax rates apply: nil up to $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% from $45,001 to $135,000, 37% from $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. Medicare levy is generally 2% (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds are not yet confirmed). Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for an estimate.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Real Estate Salary: From Hourly to Annual

If you work in real estate—whether as a property manager, sales agent, or leasing consultant—you may be paid by the hour or offered a salary. Converting between the two helps you compare job offers and understand your total compensation. This guide explains how to calculate your annual real estate salary from an hourly rate, using a standard 38-hour week and a 52-week year.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks.

For a full-time employee working 38 hours each week, the formula becomes:

Annual real estate salary = hourly rate × 38 × 52.

This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. It also assumes you take the full 52 weeks of the year (i.e., paid leave is included in the hourly rate). If your hours vary, you can use an average.

### Example: Converting a Real Estate Hourly Rate

Suppose you earn $35 per hour as a real estate assistant. Your annual salary before tax and super would be:

$35 × 38 × 52 = $69,160.

Your fortnightly gross pay would be $35 × 38 × 2 = $2,660. Knowing your fortnightly amount helps with budgeting and comparing to salary offers that are often quoted per year or per fortnight.

### National Minimum Wage vs. Award Rates vs. Real Estate Salary

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive at least $33.05 per hour including the 25% casual loading. However, many real estate employees are covered by an award (such as the Real Estate Industry Award) which may set higher minimum rates for classifications like property manager or sales representative. Award rates often include allowances and penalty rates not captured by this simple conversion. Always check your award using [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

### Industry Average vs. Your Real Estate Salary

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time employees in the rental, hiring and real estate industry as $1,979.6 per week (May 2026). This is an industry average, not a job median. It includes all roles and experience levels. Your real estate salary may be higher or lower depending on your specific job, location, and experience. Use our [reference tables](/data) to compare broader pay data.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you are a casual real estate employee, your hourly rate should already include the 25% casual loading. Do not add loading on top of a rate that already includes it. Our [the timesheet](/) calculator has a checkbox to add 25% casual loading to a base rate—use it only if your base rate does not already include loading.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a $69,160 annual real estate salary, your employer would contribute an extra $8,299.20 in super. This is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional benefit.

### Tax on Your Real Estate Salary

Your annual real estate salary is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. (The 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed in this estimate, so we use the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds for estimates.)

For a $69,160 annual real estate salary, your tax would be approximately:

- $0 on first $18,200
- 15% on $26,800 ($18,201 to $45,000) = $4,020
- 30% on $24,160 ($45,001 to $69,160) = $7,248
- Total tax = $11,268
- Medicare levy (2%) = $1,383.20
- Total deductions = $12,651.20
- Net annual pay ≈ $56,508.80

Your fortnightly take-home pay would be about $2,173.42. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a precise estimate.

### Important Notes and Limitations

This conversion is an estimate. It does not account for:
- Unpaid overtime or penalty rates
- Allowances or commissions (common in real estate sales)
- Salary sacrifice arrangements
- HELP or HECS repayments
- Medicare levy surcharge (if applicable)

Always refer to your employment contract and the Fair Work Ombudsman for your actual entitlements. The National Minimum Wage is set by the Fair Work Commission. The Australian Taxation Office provides official tax tables.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) calculator lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. It then shows your annual, fortnightly, and weekly gross pay, plus estimated tax and super. Remember: never enter a rate that already includes casual loading into the base field—use the checkbox instead.

### Summary

To find your annual real estate salary from an hourly rate:

1. Multiply your hourly rate by 38 (hours per week) and by 52 (weeks per year).
2. Add 12% super on top (up to the cap).
3. Deduct estimated tax and Medicare levy for net pay.

For a real estate salary of $35 per hour, that’s $69,160 gross, plus $8,299 super, and around $56,509 net per year. Your fortnightly gross is $2,660. Use this as a starting point to negotiate or compare job offers. For more detailed data, see our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) and [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) guides.
